description: Data + domain foundation for the Reassign decision, with NO UI changes. Extends view-model types, adds the reassign API wrapper and the identity-search helper, threads a SearchApi through PluginRuntime, adds reassign comment presets/labels, and makes the explicit, documented metrics/priority decision that a reassigned item is 'resolved' (counts as reviewed, excluded from kept/removed, sinks out of the queue). This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 (the UI). Everything here is independently unit-testable without rendering a component. Leaves the codebase building and green on its own.
steps: src/sailpoint/types.ts: add 'reassign' to the DecisionChoice union. Add a recipient view model `export interface IdentityOption { id: string; displayName: string; email: string }`. Add a `reassigned: boolean` field to ReviewItemVM (keep the existing `decision: CertificationDecision | null` for keep/remove) with a comment that `reassigned` marks an item resolved by reassignment — a THIRD outcome distinct from APPROVE/REVOKE. Set it in toReviewItemVM (default false; map from item.reassigned if present, else false).

src/sailpoint/certifications.ts: import `{ ReassignReferenceTypeEnum }` as a VALUE from 'sailpoint-api-client/certifications/api' (next to the existing `CertificationDecision` value import) and the `ReviewReassign` type. Add `export async function reassignReviewItem(api, { certificationId, itemId, reassignToId, reason })` following the exact style of `decide`/`signOff`: build `const reviewReassign: ReviewReassign = { reassign: [{ id: itemId, type: ReassignReferenceTypeEnum.Item }], reassignTo: reassignToId, reason }`, call `const res = await api.reassignIdentityCertificationsV1({ id: certificationId, reviewReassign })`, return `toCampaignVM(res.data)`, and wrap any throw in `toFriendlyError`. Define a `ReassignInput` interface in the same documented style as `DecisionInput`.

src/sailpoint/identities.ts (NEW): import `{ Index, SearchApi }` from 'sailpoint-api-client/search/api' and `toFriendlyError`, `FriendlyError` from './certifications' (or move toFriendlyError if a cycle appears — prefer importing). Add `buildIdentityQuery(raw)` and `escapeSearchTerm` adapted from org-graph/src/data/sailpoint-directory.ts (fields: firstName, lastName, email, emailAddress, attributes.firstname, attributes.lastname, attributes.email; each whitespace-split term wrapped as (field:*term* OR ...) joined by AND). Add `export async function searchIdentities(api: SearchApi, rawQuery: string): Promise<IdentityOption[]>` that returns [] for a query shorter than 2 non-space chars, otherwise calls `api.searchPostV1({ search: { indices: [Index.Identities], query: { query }, sort: ['name'] }, limit: 25, count: false })`, maps each untyped row to IdentityOption with defensive reads (id; displayName from row.displayName || row.name || attributes.displayName; email from row.email || row.emailAddress || attributes.email), drops rows with no id, and wraps throws in toFriendlyError. Keep defensive helpers small and commented (study org-graph map-identity.ts for the pattern, trimmed to 3 fields).

src/sailpoint/sdkClient.ts: import `SearchApi` from 'sailpoint-api-client' (root, same place CertificationsApi comes from), add `searchApi: SearchApi` to the `PluginRuntime` interface, and in `initPlugin` build `const searchApi = new SearchApi(configuration)` from the SAME `configuration` object already used for certificationsApi/summariesApi, returning it on the runtime. Do NOT change the handshake/eager-SDK logic.

src/domain/language.ts: DECISION_LABEL, DECISION_MEANING, and CANNED_COMMENTS are `Record<DecisionChoice, ...>`, so add a `reassign` entry to each. Label: 'Reassign'. Meaning: a plain sentence such as 'Someone else will review this item. It leaves your list once you reassign it.' CANNED_COMMENTS.reassign (plain, non-technical): ['This isn\'t my direct report.', 'This belongs to another manager.', 'A subject-matter expert should review this.', 'I\'m covering while this person is on leave.'].

src/domain/metrics.ts: in computeMetrics, treat a reassigned item (item.reassigned === true, or item.completed) as counting toward `reviewed`/`remaining`/`percentComplete` but NOT toward `approved` or `revoked`. Add a comment: reassignment is resolved from THIS reviewer's perspective (recommended decision), so it advances progress but is a third outcome, neither kept nor removed. Keep the items-vs-campaign-counts fallback intact.

src/domain/priority.ts: in `prioritize`, treat a reassigned item as resolved so it sinks to the bottom alongside completed items (introduce a small `isResolved(item) = item.completed || item.reassigned` predicate and use it where `completed` currently gates ordering). In `countByPriority`, exclude reassigned items from the outstanding tally the same way completed items are excluded. Comment the rationale.
acceptance_criteria: `npx vitest run src/sailpoint src/domain` passes, including new tests for reassignReviewItem (builds the correct ReviewReassign with type 'ITEM' and reassignTo/reason, maps the DTO via toCampaignVM, maps HTTP errors to FriendlyError) and searchIdentities (builds a contains query across name+email fields, returns [] for blank/<2-char input, maps rows to {id,displayName,email}, drops id-less rows, wraps errors).
`npx vitest run src/sailpoint/sdkClient.test.ts` passes with searchApi present on the runtime (test updated if it asserts the runtime shape).
metrics.test.ts and language.test.ts updated so a reassigned item counts as reviewed-but-not-kept/removed and the reassign presets/labels exist, and both pass.
No UI/component files are modified in this feature.

`npm run build` type-checks the whole project (the new union member and types compile; UI call sites that will consume them in FEAT-002 are not yet referenced, so no dangling references are introduced).
findings:
FEAT-002 wiring reference.

EXPORTED SIGNATURES:
- reassignReviewItem(api: CertificationsApi, input: ReassignInput): Promise<CampaignVM>  — src/sailpoint/certifications.ts. ReassignInput = { certificationId: string; itemId: string; reassignToId: string; reason: string }. Builds ReviewReassign { reassign: [{ id: itemId, type: ReassignReferenceTypeEnum.Item ('ITEM') }], reassignTo: reassignToId, reason }, calls api.reassignIdentityCertificationsV1({ id: certificationId, reviewReassign }), returns toCampaignVM(res.data). Throws FriendlyError. NOTE: unlike decide() which takes (api, campaignId, decisions[]), reassign takes a single ReassignInput object that already carries certificationId.
- searchIdentities(api: SearchApi, rawQuery: string): Promise<IdentityOption[]>  — src/sailpoint/identities.ts. Returns [] when rawQuery has <2 non-space chars (never calls the API). Otherwise searchPostV1({ search: { indices: [Index.Identities], query: { query }, sort: ['name'] }, limit: 25, count: false }). Maps rows defensively; drops rows without id; throws FriendlyError. Also exports buildIdentityQuery(raw) and re-exports FriendlyError.
- IdentityOption (src/sailpoint/types.ts) = { id: string; displayName: string; email: string }. displayName/email may be '' when the row lacked those fields — the picker should handle empty strings.

ReviewItemVM.reassigned FLAG:
- Added `reassigned: boolean` to ReviewItemVM (src/sailpoint/types.ts), REQUIRED (not optional). Distinct third outcome from decision (APPROVE/REVOKE). toReviewItemVM defaults it false and reads item.reassigned defensively ((item as {reassigned?:boolean}).reassigned === true) since the generated AccessReviewItem has no such field.
- Because the field is required, every ReviewItemVM fixture must set it. I added `reassigned: false` to the test factories in: components/DecisionDialog.test.tsx, components/DrillDownTable.test.tsx, components/ReviewQueue.test.tsx, state/useDecisions.test.ts, views/CampaignDashboard.test.tsx (no component source changed — fixtures only). FEAT-002's optimistic updater (useReviewItems.applyReassign) should set reassigned:true on the item.

DOMAIN:
- DecisionChoice union = 'allow' | 'remove' | 'reassign'. language.ts DECISION_LABEL.reassign='Reassign', DECISION_MEANING.reassign set, CANNED_COMMENTS.reassign has 4 plain presets.
- metrics.computeMetrics: a reassigned item counts toward reviewed/remaining/percentComplete but NOT approved/revoked.
- priority.ts: new isResolved(item)=item.completed||item.reassigned gates both prioritize() ordering (reassigned sinks) and countByPriority() (reassigned excluded from outstanding tally).

NO deviations from the plan. UI/component source untouched. Verification all green: npx vitest run src/sailpoint src/domain = 45; sdkClient.test.ts = 2; npm run build OK; npm run lint clean; full npm test = 80 (baseline 67 + 13 new).
